text: This is DVote: secret-ballot elections whose count anyone can check. Here is one anonymous election, from start to finish, on a local test chain.
The organiser connects a wallet and creates the election. Its title, candidates and schedule are fixed in a smart contract.
Every step follows the contract's schedule. On this local chain, we move the clock forward instead of waiting.
A student registers. Their browser makes a voting key, and they confirm their institute email. No wallet, no cryptocurrency.
Only a public code made from the key goes to the registrar. The key itself never leaves this browser.
When registration closes, the registrar publishes the voter list by itself. The list goes on IPFS, and its fingerprint is fixed in the contract.
Once its time has come, anyone can open voting.
The student picks a candidate. Their browser proves they are on the list, without revealing which voter they are.
A relayer checks the proof and pays the fee. The ballot is on the blockchain, and counted.
Opening the booth again shows they have voted. The same key cannot vote twice.
When voting ends, anyone can close it and finalize the result.
The result is final. Each ballot is listed by its ballot ID alone, never by who cast it.
Finally, anyone can audit the election. The browser recounts every ballot from the blockchain and IPFS alone.
Every check passed: the voter list, every proof, the count and the winner.
DVote. Anonymous ballots, and a count anyone can check.
